primary_sources_read.finding: Actual held cover verifies Selim Ghazouani, Structures affines complexes sur les surfaces de Riemann, Université Paris Sciences et Lettres, 2017. Actual physical pages, not drifting extraction segments, were read for the foliation, area forms, angle restrictions and three accepted targets.

Ghazouani–Pirio primary: leaves of M_1,n have complex hyperbolic dimension n−1 and holonomy in PU(1,n−1). Finite-holonomy leaves have finite-volume cone-manifold completions; the displayed arithmetic examples do not classify all holonomy lattices. This explicitly confirms repair of thesis introduction PU(1,n) indexing.

Primary analytic treatment computes genus-one two-marked-point leaves and volume finiteness in special cases. Distinct connected components occur even for n=2; it does not classify every finite-holonomy leaf for all n or prove all-genus volume finiteness.

Yu–Zhong, submitted 10 September 2026: introduction explicitly states that a general discreteness criterion for arbitrary Ghazouani–Pirio monodromy groups remains unknown. Its theorem classifies commensurability relations of the sixteen known arithmetic examples, not all lattices or all connected components.

Published primary Theorem 4 distinguishes H = limit set minus parabolic fixed points from the full limit set. Directions in the complement within the limit set are totally periodic; hence the literal thesis Conjectures 3/5 saying every parameter in the full limit set is minimal are false. The still conjectural nonparabolic refinement is not silently substituted.

Boulanger–Ghazouani–Tahar, published Geometry & Topology29(2025): closed-geodesic directions on every dilation surface are dense; this answers the existence-of-cylinder conjecture. Source p.27 explicitly identifies a closed geodesic with membership in a cylinder.

Bande primary Theorem2.1 recalls Calabi: a generic closed ordinary 1-form is intrinsically harmonic iff locally harmonic and transitive. Saddle zeros alone do not state the global transitivity condition. Twisted Question7 / equivalent foliation Question6 held at the trivial-holonomy countercase and scope gates rather than declared open.

accepted.title: Finiteness of Veech volume
accepted.text: Let M_{g,n} be the moduli orbifold of genus-g compact Riemann surfaces with n ordered, distinct marked points. For θ=(θ₁,…,θ_n) with θ_i>0 and Σ_i(2π−θ_i)=2π(2−2g), identify M_{g,n} with flat Euclidean cone metrics of those angles, up to homothety, by choosing their conformal classes. The Veech foliation fixes the rotational holonomy character ρ:π₁(Σ minus the marked points)→U(1), where a small positive loop δ_i has ρ(δ_i)=exp(iθ_i). Assume 2g−2+n>0 and no θ_i is in 2πℤ. Define Ω_θ by pairing the transverse symplectic volume on the holonomy-character torus (the form induced by the intersection pairing on H¹(Σ;ℝ)) with each leaf’s invariant volume from the projectivized Hermitian area form. Concretely, local leaf coordinates are complex edge vectors of a polygonal flat-surface model satisfying the fixed rotational gluing equations and polygon closure; total signed triangle area is a Hermitian form A, and the coordinates are projectivized on A>0. Its projective unitary homogeneous structure supplies the leaf volume, while holonomy coordinates supply the transverse volume. Is ∫_{M_{g,n}} Ω_θ finite for every such g,n,θ?
accepted.subject: Differential Geometry & Geometric Analysis
accepted.scope_review: Actual physical76–83 defines holonomy, pure mapping-class quotient, projective Hermitian area and transverse symplectic volume. Gauss–Bonnet and nonintegral cone angles are retained. No replacement by the integer-angle Masur–Veech measure; no restriction to genus-one hyperbolic leaves. A fixed positive normalization of invariant volume does not change finiteness.
accepted.literature_finding: 2016/2019 primary only establishes special genus-one cases. Dated current primary scan found no all-genus / arbitrary admissible-angle resolution; this is a bounded status assessment.

accepted.title: Lattice holonomy of flat-torus isoholonomic leaves
accepted.text: Fix n≥2 and rational angles θ_i∈2πℚ with Σ_iθ_i=2πn, 2π<θ₁<4π, and 0<θ_i<2π for i>1. Let T_{1,n} parametrize marked conformal tori with n ordered points and their associated area-one flat cone metrics of angles θ. Let hol:T_{1,n}→Hom(π₁(Σ_{1,n}),U(1)) assign rotational holonomy, with hol(δ_i)=exp(iθ_i). For ρ in its image, let F_[ρ] be the image of hol⁻¹(ρ) in M_{1,n}=T_{1,n}/PMod_{1,n}, where PMod consists of mapping classes fixing each marked point. F_[ρ] may be disconnected. Each connected component C inherits a complex hyperbolic structure of dimension n−1 from the projectivized Hermitian area form in polygon-period coordinates. Classify the pairs (θ,ρ) and components C for which the image of the resulting holonomy representation π₁^orb(C)→PU(1,n−1) is discrete and has finite covolume. In particular, does any such component have nonarithmetic lattice holonomy?
accepted.subject: Differential Geometry & Geometric Analysis
accepted.scope_review: Actual physical24 fixes the rational-angle hyperbolic regime and complex dimension n−1; physical76–77 defines quotient by pure mapping classes and allows disconnected leaves. Thesis introduction writes PU(1,n), an indexing error explicitly repaired to PU(1,n−1) using its preceding dimension statement and primary1604.01812. No finite-image restriction is invented for this general classification question; ρ is realizable. Orbifold π₁ accommodates source quotient stabilizers.
accepted.literature_finding: 2026 primary2609.11482 expressly retains the unknown general discreteness criterion; its sixteen arithmetic commensurability classifications are partial and do not answer this full lattice/nonarithmetic question.

accepted.title: Connected components of finite-holonomy flat-torus leaves
accepted.text: Fix n≥2 and rational angles θ_i∈2πℚ with Σ_iθ_i=2πn, 2π<θ₁<4π, and 0<θ_i<2π for i>1. Let T_{1,n} parametrize marked conformal tori with n ordered points and their associated area-one flat cone metrics of angles θ. Let hol:T_{1,n}→Hom(π₁(Σ_{1,n}),U(1)) assign rotational holonomy, with hol(δ_i)=exp(iθ_i). For ρ in its image, let F_[ρ] be the image of hol⁻¹(ρ) in M_{1,n}=T_{1,n}/PMod_{1,n}, where PMod consists of mapping classes fixing each marked point. F_[ρ] may be disconnected. Under the additional assumption that Im(ρ) is finite, determine all connected components of F_[ρ] for arbitrary n,θ,ρ in this range. Equivalently, determine its set π₀(F_[ρ]) in terms of these data.
accepted.subject: Differential Geometry & Geometric Analysis
accepted.scope_review: Actual physical127 discusses F_θ(M) before explicitly fixing finite Imρ; physical125–127 finite-holonomy algebraic-leaf context and physical77 warns that a named leaf can be disconnected.
